channel.title: The Washington Informer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Washington Informer (washingtoninformer.com)

item.title: City Cruises and OCTFME Celebrate District Culture with Capital Sound Series
item.description: Celebrate D.C. culture and the spring equinox aboard the Odyssey with the Capital Sound Series, showcasing local artists and the city's beauty.

item.title: Black Press Week: Tradition, Technology, Rising Talent
item.description: Black Press Day 2026 at Howard University celebrates 199 years of the Black Press, highlighting excellence, legacy, and truth-telling.

item.title: TILGHMAN: The Real Work Begins After the IEP Meeting
item.description: Discover the challenges faced by parents of autistic children when following up on legally binding plans. A call for a system that keeps its promises.

item.title: What's Really Driving Energy Costs: Pepco Points to Causes and Solutions
item.description: Discover why energy bills in Washington, D.C. are rising and learn about the relief efforts Pepco is providing to help customers manage the costs.

item.title: Washington Performing Arts Celebrates 60 Years, Highlights Transformational Power of Supporting Artists
item.description: Washington Performing Arts celebrated its 60th anniversary with a gala showcasing the power of the arts in uniting and transforming lives.

item.title: Nationals Secure 10-4 Victory Over Chicago Cubs on MLB Opening Day
item.description: Washington Nationals triumph over Chicago Cubs 10-4 in MLB opener, with home runs and a milestone victory for manager Blake Butera.

item.title: Live Boldly – April 2026 Message from Department of Aging and Community Living
item.description: April is a time to focus on health, balance, and community. Learn about managing stress, staying connected, and caring for the environment.

item.title: UConn Defeats Duke With Mullins' Last-Second 3-Pointer, Advances to Final Four
item.description: UConn stages a stunning 19-point comeback to defeat Duke and advance to the NCAA Final Four. Braylon Mullins hits game-winning shot.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Russell Simmons Files Explosive Manhattan Lawsuit Against HBO
item.description: Russell Simmons accuses HBO and partners of ignoring warnings, burying evidence, and defaming him in a lawsuit over the documentary 'On the Record.'

item.title: More Than 120 Nations Support UN Measure Declaring Slavery 'Gravest Crime Against Humanity'
item.description: U.S. aligns with Israel and Argentina to vote against U.N. resolution recognizing transatlantic slave trade as gravest crime against humanity.

item.title: New Data Shows Women Still Earn Just 81 Cents on the Dollar, With Steeper Gaps for Black Women and Latinas
item.description: New data shows that women working full time, year-round continue to be paid less than men in every state, with wider disparities affecting women of color.

item.title: Metrorail at 50: Free Rides for Students and Questions About Federal Presence
item.description: The Washington Metro Area Transit Authority (WMATA) has distributed 450,000 Kids Ride Free SmarTrip cards to help young people navigate public transit free of charge, providing a critical resource for District families and allowing students to access extracurricular activities and jobs.

item.title: Psalmayene 24 to Direct a Stacked Cast in Production of Ossie Davis' Civil Rights-Era Classic
item.description: Studio Theatre has announced the full cast and creative team for its upcoming production of "Purlie Victorious," Ossie Davis' 1961 civil rights-era farce, featuring a nine-member cast led by Warner Miller and Danaya Esperanza, and directed by Psalmayene 24.

item.title: D.C. Secures More Than $302K for Workers in Misclassification Crackdown
item.description: Over 100 construction workers in D.C. to receive restitution as drywall companies settle with the Attorney General for misclassifying employees.

item.title: Motorists Feel the Sting as Gas Prices Rise Above $4 Per Gallon
item.description: Rising fuel costs are hitting drivers hard as gas prices surge due to Middle East tensions, impacting household budgets and small businesses.
